newsitem.title: NORWAY: Sparebankgruppen asked to review bid for Fokus.
newsitem.headline: Sparebankgruppen asked to review bid for Fokus.

text.p: The Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission on Tuesday asked Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 savings banks, to consider withdrawing its takeover bid for Fokus Bank.

The commission said Sparebankgruppen would probably not win acceptance for its bid from 67 percent of shareholders in Fokus. The figure is the minimum amount required to change the statutes of a company in Norway.

Sparebankgruppen on June 6 announced it was extending by six weeks its 73 crowns per share bid to shareholders in Fokus and said it controlled 51 percent of Norway's fourth largest bank. The new deadline was set for July 18.
Fokus, which is fighting what it perceives as a hostile takeover bid, has criticised Sparebankgruppen for extending its bid for such a long period of time.

"Against this background, especially because of the uncertainty that this long period of time could mean for all parties affected, the commission would like Sparebankgruppen to consider the situation anew with a view to withdrawing the bid," the commission said in a letter to the group.
Sparebankgruppen said it was taking the recommendation seriously and would come up with an answer soon, possibly this week.
Fokus has recommended its shareholders to turn down the bid by Sparebankgruppen, which wants to carve up Fokus among its members.
